questions.question: A company needs to ingest clickstream events in real time, store them durably for 7 days, and run a Lambda function to enrich each event. The Lambda occasionally fails and must reprocess specific records. Which service as source?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Kinesis Data Streams supports replay — records persist up to 365 days, consumers re-read by iterator. A is wrong — Firehose does NOT support replay once delivered. B is wrong — S3 notifications are not a replayable stream. D is wrong — same reason as B.

questions.question: A pipeline reads from Kinesis and calls a third-party API (100 req/s limit) for each record, but the stream receives 500 records/second. Best approach?
options: B. Use SQS as a buffer between Kinesis and Lambda
C. Use Firehose to batch before calling the API
questions.explanation: B is correct. SQS buffers and decouples — Lambda drains at controlled rate under 100 req/s. A is wrong — more shards increases read throughput but not throttle downstream. C is wrong — Firehose cannot call custom REST APIs. D is wrong — fan-out improves read throughput, not rate limiting.

questions.question: Migrate on-premises Oracle to Aurora PostgreSQL with minimal downtime and schema conversion. Which combination?
options: A. DMS only, manual schema conversion
B. DMS with DMS Schema Conversion
C. DataSync for data, Glue for schema
questions.explanation: B is correct. DMS Schema Conversion (replaced retired SCT) converts schemas; DMS does CDC for near-zero downtime. A is error-prone. C — DataSync is for files, not DBs. D — SCT is retired.

questions.question: Pipeline must run every weekday 8 AM Asia/Tokyo, with retry, 15-min flexible window, and DLQ. Which service?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Scheduler supports timezone-aware cron, flexible windows, retry, and DLQ. A lacks flexible windows/DLQ. C is UTC-only. D is overkill for a daily trigger.

questions.question: Serverless pipeline: ingest API request, validate, call third-party API, write to DynamoDB in order. Which service?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Step Functions is serverless, supports ordering via Map state on SQS FIFO. A — Lambda is concurrent, no order guarantee. B — MWAA is for complex DAGs. D — Glue Workflows only orchestrate Glue jobs/crawlers.

questions.question: MSK Standard cluster at 85% CPU during peak. Team worries about rebalancing failures. What to do?
options: C. Scale up brokers to keep CPU under 60%
questions.explanation: C is correct. Best practice: keep MSK CPU under 60% for rebalancing/recovery headroom. A — Express is different architecture. B — more partitions doesn't reduce per-broker CPU. D — no auto-scaling for Standard brokers.

questions.question: Glue ETL reads JSON from S3, writes Parquet, but reprocesses everything daily. How to optimize?
questions.explanation: A is correct. Job bookmarks track processed S3 objects so only new/changed files are read. B — 15-min timeout. C — more ops, same reprocessing issue. D — reinventing bookmarks.

questions.question: Lambda processes Kinesis records but fails on individual records, causing entire batch retry and duplicates. Best fix?
options: D. Move to Glue streaming ETL
questions.explanation: A is correct. BisectBatchOnFunctionError isolates bad records; DestinationConfig sends failures to DLQ. B — more timeout doesn't prevent duplicate retries. C — improves throughput, not error handling. D — different architecture.

questions.question: Deliver streaming data to 3 S3 buckets and OpenSearch, each with different transformations. Which service?
options: B. Kinesis Firehose + multiple delivery streams
questions.explanation: B is correct. Firehose supports multiple delivery streams, each with its own Lambda transform and destination. A requires building consumers. C is more complex. D doesn't do continuous stream delivery.

questions.question: Scheduled Salesforce-to-S3 integration with field-level mapping and data masking. Which service?
options: A. Glue ETL with custom connectors
questions.explanation: C is correct. AppFlow is purpose-built for no-code SaaS-to-AWS integration with mapping, masking, scheduled/incremental flows. A requires custom code. B doesn't do SaaS extraction. D is for DB migration.

questions.question: 10,000 independent executions/second, each under 5 minutes. Step Functions Standard or Express?
options: B. Express for high throughput and low cost
questions.explanation: B is correct. Express supports up to 100K starts/sec, cheaper — ideal for high-throughput short-lived workloads. A scales slower. C doesn't solve throughput. D — Express lacks visual debugging.

questions.question: Need 5-minute tumbling window aggregations over Kinesis stream before writing to S3. Which service?
options: A. Lambda tumbling window event source
questions.explanation: C is correct. Managed Flink natively supports tumbling/sliding/session windows — purpose-built for stateful stream processing. A has 5-min max and less efficient state. B is delivery timing, not aggregation. D doesn't process streams.

questions.question: Glue job writes small Parquet files (<1 MB) causing slow Athena queries. Most cost-effective fix?
options: A. Athena CTAS to rewrite table
B. Glue compaction job to merge files
questions.explanation: B is correct. Compaction directly addresses small-file problem cost-effectively. A is full table rewrite. C doesn't change file size. D — format isn't the issue.

questions.question: Raw JSON in S3 causes slow expensive Athena queries. What to do?
options: B. Convert to Parquet and add partitioning
questions.explanation: B is correct. Parquet enables column pruning and predicate pushdown; partitioning enables partition pruning — both reduce data scanned. A doesn't affect query speed. C reduces storage cost only. D doesn't fix scanning JSON.

questions.question: Need idempotent Kinesis consumer so reprocessing doesn't create duplicates. Best approach?
options: A. Kinesis sequence numbers as partition keys in DynamoDB with ConditionExpression
questions.explanation: A is correct. Sequence numbers as partition keys + put-if-absent condition ensures idempotent writes. B doesn't prevent record-level duplicates. C doesn't provide exactly-once. D has no deduplication.

questions.question: MWAA DAG fails intermittently due to Glue job timeout. First troubleshooting step?
options: B. Check CloudWatch Logs for Glue driver/executor logs
questions.explanation: B is correct. CloudWatch Logs show OOM, skew, or insufficient DPUs — the first diagnostic. A affects scheduler, not Glue execution. C doesn't diagnose. D tracks processed files, not timeouts.

questions.question: Transform CSV files from on-premises SFTP into Parquet on S3. Which services?
questions.explanation: A is correct. Transfer Family manages SFTP ingestion into S3; Glue ETL handles CSV-to-Parquet. B — DMS is for DBs. C — EMR is overkill for format conversion. D — S3 events don't pull from SFTP.

questions.question: Team wants schema evolution, time travel, and ACID transactions on a data lake without managing Iceberg infrastructure. Which service?
questions.explanation: C is correct. S3 Tables is fully managed Iceberg on S3 — schema evolution, time travel, ACID without self-managing. A requires ops effort. B is metadata only. D is a warehouse, not a lake table format.

questions.question: Redshift cluster has uneven query performance. Some slices have much more data. Cause and fix?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Uneven DISTKEY causes data skew across slices. A adds query capacity, not distribution. C has same distribution concepts. D queries S3 externally.

questions.question: DynamoDB table with TTL attribute. Want to trigger Lambda when items expire. How?
options: A. DynamoDB TTL directly triggers Lambda
B. Enable Streams, filter for TTL delete events
D. CloudWatch Events on DynamoDB metrics
questions.explanation: B is correct. TTL deletes generate stream records (userIdentity: service.amazonaws.com). Lambda filters these. A — TTL has no direct Lambda trigger. C — no native TTL events. D — metrics don't trigger per-item.

questions.question: Query S3 data and live Aurora PostgreSQL from a single query. Which approach?
options: A. DMS to replicate Aurora to S3, then Athena
B. Redshift Federated Query to Aurora
C. Athena Federated Query via Lambda
questions.explanation: B is correct. Redshift Federated Query pushes SQL to Aurora via JDBC, joining Spectrum (S3) with live Aurora. A has replication latency. C exists but less performant. D eliminates ad-hoc flexibility.

questions.question: Give analytics team read-only access to specific columns in a Glue Data Catalog table. Which service?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Lake Formation provides column-level and row-level (LF-Tags) grants. A operates at service/resource level. C tracks configuration. D discovers PII.

questions.question: Implement vector similarity search on existing PostgreSQL data. Which service?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Aurora pgvector supports HNSW/IVF indexes — best when you already have PostgreSQL. A is a separate system. C is for graphs. D is for RAG.

questions.question: Glue crawler is slow re-crawling entire S3 prefix daily. How to optimize?
options: B. Use incremental crawling and partition projection
C. Replace with manual Catalog API calls
questions.explanation: B is correct. Incremental crawling processes only new/changed objects; partition projection infers partitions without crawling. A doesn't fix full re-crawling. C requires more dev effort. D doesn't solve per-run performance.

questions.question: Share live Redshift data with another AWS account without copying. Which feature?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Data Sharing provides live, no-copy sharing between clusters/accounts. A is point-in-time copies. B queries S3, not live Redshift. D has latency.

questions.question: S3 data: Standard 30 days, then Standard-IA, Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year, delete after 7 years. What to configure?
options: A. S3 Lifecycle policy with multiple rules
B. S3 Event Notifications with Lambda
questions.explanation: A is correct. A single lifecycle policy with multiple transition actions and expiration. B doesn't support time-based actions. C evaluates compliance. D is for one-time bulk operations.

questions.question: Comparing HNSW vs IVF vector indexes. Which is correct?
options: A. HNSW is more memory-efficient but slower
B. IVF supports incremental updates better
C. HNSW is graph-based, fast, memory-intensive; IVF clusters vectors, more memory-efficient
D. IVF always has better recall
questions.explanation: C is correct. HNSW: graph-based, fast, memory-hungry. IVF: k-means clusters, scans nearest, more memory-efficient, lower recall. A — opposite. B — HNSW supports incremental better. D — HNSW typically has better recall.

questions.question: A Redshift materialized view refreshes every 30 minutes. Analysts query it frequently. The base table receives continuous INSERTs. What is the best practice?
options: A. Use a scheduled Redshift query to recreate the view
C. Use CTAS instead of materialized views
D. Query the base table directly
questions.explanation: B is correct. Auto-refresh materialized views update incrementally when the base table changes — more efficient than full rebuild. A is manual and slower. C requires full rewrite each time. D defeats the purpose of pre-computed results.

questions.question: An application needs sub-millisecond reads with strong consistency and durability. The dataset fits in memory. Which service?
questions.explanation: B is correct. MemoryDB provides sub-ms latency, strong consistency (unlike ElastiCache Redis), and durability (multi-AZ). A — DAX provides microsecond cache but DynamoDB itself is single-digit ms. C — Memcached is not durable and has eventual consistency. D — Aurora is ms-level, not sub-ms.

questions.question: A Glue crawler adds a new column to an existing table. Downstream Athena queries fail with "column not found". Why?
options: A. Crawler schema change policy is set to IGNORE
B. Athena engine cache is stale
C. The column is in a nested JSON field not supported by Athena
D. Glue Data Catalog requires manual table update for schema changes
questions.explanation: A is correct. If schema change policy is IGNORE, the crawler detects but doesn't apply the new column to the catalog. Set to UPDATE_IN_DATABASE to apply changes. B is unlikely for new column errors. C would show a different error. D is false — crawlers do update schemas when configured.

questions.question: A Glue ETL job fails with OutOfMemoryError on the executor. First thing to check?
options: B. Check Spark UI for data skew and shuffle spill
questions.explanation: B is correct. Spark UI shows task distribution, shuffle, and memory usage to identify skew causing OOM. A adds resources without diagnosing. C tracks processed files. D is a different platform.

questions.question: EMR Spark job is slow. Spark History Server shows one task 10x longer than others. What is this?
questions.explanation: B is correct. One long task in a stage is classic data skew. Fix with salting or broadcast join. A unlikely as single-task skew. C does not address root cause. D would affect all tasks.

questions.question: Detect anomalies in Kinesis IteratorAge metric without static thresholds. Which CloudWatch feature?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Anomaly Detection uses ML to set expected bands and alerts on deviation. A combines metrics mathematically. C combines alarms. D identifies top contributors.

questions.question: Profile a 500 GB dataset for distributions, missing values, and outliers before ETL. Which service?
questions.explanation: B is correct. DataBrew provides visual data profiling — statistics, distributions, missing values, outliers — without code. A requires SQL for each stat. C is for dashboards. D is for quality rules.

questions.question: Step Functions execution failed at state 3. Need input/output of each state to debug. Where?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Execution History records input/output, status, timing for every state. A lacks structured state I/O. C is out of scope. D is not a Step Functions feature.

questions.question: Ad-hoc SQL queries on S3 data and prototype ETL with Spark. Serverless, pay-per-use. Which service?
questions.explanation: D is correct. Athena notebooks provide Jupyter-like serverless Spark — pay per DPU-second. A requires cluster management. B is for batch jobs. C is for production ETL.

questions.question: Pipeline generates millions of small log files daily. CloudWatch Logs is expensive. Cost-effective long-term storage and analysis?
options: A. Keep all in CloudWatch Logs
B. Subscription filter to Firehose to S3, query with Athena
C. Manual export to S3 daily
questions.explanation: B is correct. Subscription filter to Firehose then S3 is automated; Athena provides cheap SQL querying. A is expensive. C is manual. D is expensive for archival.

questions.question: Glue Data Quality finds 5% NULL in a required column. Want to fail the job when threshold exceeded. How?
options: A. Custom Lambda check after job
B. DQDL ruleset with isComplete rule, fail on violation
C. CloudWatch alarm on Glue metrics
D. Athena validation after each run
questions.explanation: B is correct. DQDL rules like isComplete with thresholds, job fails on violation. A is manual. C requires custom metric extraction. D is post-hoc.

questions.question: Glue ETL job reads from JDBC (Aurora) and gets intermittent connection timeouts. Most likely cause?
options: B. No RDS Proxy — connection storms exhaust connections
questions.explanation: B is correct. Without RDS Proxy, multiple executors opening JDBC connections can exhaust Aurora. RDS Proxy pools connections. A is possible but less likely. C affects speed not JDBC. D is unrelated.

questions.question: Redshift query slow. STL_QUERY shows high wlm_queue_time in default queue. What and how to fix?
options: B. Waiting for WLM slot — increase concurrency or use concurrency scaling
questions.explanation: B is correct. High wlm_queue_time means waiting for a slot. Fix: increase WLM concurrency or enable concurrency scaling. A shows high execution time not queue time. C is for S3 data. D fixes bloat not queuing.

questions.question: QuickSight BI dashboards with ML-powered anomaly detection and forecasting without building models. Which feature?
questions.explanation: B is correct. ML Insights provides built-in anomaly detection, forecasting, narratives. A is for embedding. C is scheduled reports. D is in-memory storage.

questions.question: A data engineer needs to encrypt S3 objects at rest using a customer-managed key, and the key must be rotated automatically every year. Which KMS feature?
options: B. Customer managed CMK with automatic annual rotation
C. External key store with manual rotation
questions.explanation: B is correct. Customer-managed CMKs support automatic annual rotation. A does not support automatic rotation. C is manual. D reduces KMS API calls but doesn't rotate the key.

questions.question: Lake Formation grants a team SELECT on a table. They should only see rows where region = 'US'. How?
options: C. Glue ETL to create filtered views
questions.explanation: B is correct. LF-Tags enable row-level access control in Lake Formation. Tag rows with region and grant access to specific tag values. A cannot filter at row level. C creates data duplication. D operates at object level.

questions.question: A company must discover PII in millions of S3 objects across hundreds of buckets. Which service automates this?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Macie uses ML + pattern matching to automatically discover and classify PII in S3. A tracks resource configuration. C scans compute. D detects threats.

questions.question: A Glue job needs a database password. The password rotates every 30 days. How should the job retrieve it?
options: A. Store in S3 and read at runtime
B. AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation
C. Parameter Store with manual rotation
D. Hardcode in Glue job parameters
questions.explanation: B is correct. Secrets Manager supports automatic rotation (native for RDS/Aurora) and the Glue job retrieves via GetSecretValue API. A has no rotation. C requires manual rotation. D is a security anti-pattern.

questions.question: An audit requires tracking all API calls that modified S3 bucket policies in the last 90 days. Which service?
questions.explanation: B is correct. CloudTrail logs all management events (including S3 policy changes) with 90-day free retention. Create a trail for longer retention. A captures Lambda logs, not API calls. C captures network traffic. D tracks resource state, not API calls.

questions.question: A data team must share S3 data with an external partner account using Lake Formation, but only specific columns. How?
options: A. S3 bucket policy with conditions
questions.explanation: B is correct. Lake Formation column-level grants allow sharing specific columns to external accounts. A cannot filter columns. C is too broad. D is for temporary individual object access.

questions.question: S3 objects must not be deleted or overwritten for 3 years after creation. Which S3 feature?
options: B. S3 Object Lock in Governance mode
C. S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode
questions.explanation: C is correct. Compliance mode prevents any user (including root) from deleting or overwriting objects until the retention period expires. A allows deletion of all versions. B allows privileged users to bypass. D prevents deletion with MFA but has no retention period.

questions.question: AWS IAM Access Analyzer generates a finding that an S3 bucket is accessible to the entire internet. The bucket contains public datasets. What should the engineer do?
options: B. Review the finding, confirm the bucket should be public, and archive the finding
questions.explanation: B is correct. Access Analyzer reports on what IS accessible, not what should be. If the bucket is intentionally public (public datasets), archive the finding as a known and accepted configuration. A breaks the use case. C destroys data. D leaves the finding active.

questions.question: A company uses S3, Redshift, and Glue. They want a centralized data governance solution with domain-based access, data lineage, and business catalog. Which service?
questions.explanation: B is correct. DataZone provides data portals, business catalog, domain-based governance, and data lineage across S3, Redshift, and Glue. A provides FGAC but not business catalogs or portals. C does not exist as a standalone service. D is IAM-level control without data governance features.
